transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Chen (Redwood SE), Mark Torres (GateBank Head of ML Ops), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Jamal Reed (Security), Anya Lopez (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC latency tuning results; reviewed TTFT numbers for streaming vs non-streaming, kernel selection experiments, and sequence-length/regression observations. Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, run kernel-level tests on p4d-equivalent nodes, GateBank to provide sample traffic and security constraints.

Topics:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) improvements with streaming + small-batch KV cache
- Kernel choices (flash-attn vs cutlass/metal kernels) and quantization impact
- Sequence length trimming and prefix caching strategies
- Dedicated vs hosted node selection and fallback behavior
- Security/KMS constraints for Private deployment

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45, quick agenda — run through the latest numbers, then Lina will walk the kernel tests, then open q's.
[00:14] Mark: yeah thanks, uh appreciate it. we've been seeing a lot of TTFT variability in the spike window, so looking to see if the streaming changes helped.
[00:28] Lina: cool, I pushed the latest run to the workbook, it's in the sheet — note that the streaming build used continuous prefix streaming and smaller micro-batches. TTFT improved about 120-150ms median on our sim traffic.
[00:45] Priya: when you say streaming build, is that the server side streaming or client chunking? we do client-side chunking too so wanted to be clear.
[00:52] Lina: server-side streaming; Redwood runtime streams token frames as soon as available and uses the KV cache to avoid recompute on repeated prefixes. client chunking adds small overhead so we tested both.
[01:08] Jamal: quick security note — any streaming has to honor our data-in-transit policies and the KMS envelope. is there any tokenization/PII leakage risk in the prefetched cache?
[01:20] Samir: good point — KV cache only stores internal model keys, not user PII. we also support envelope encryption with customer KMS in Private; we'll attach the SOC2 docs.
[01:35] Anya: also timeline — we want to get this into a pilot by mid-Oct if possible, is that still realistic?
[01:42] Samir: yes, if we close the kernel testing and get your sample traces this week next week we can turn up dedicated nodes.
[02:00] Lina: backing up to the numbers — for the 2k token context test, non-streaming median TTFT was ~480ms, streaming dropped to ~330ms. p95 stayed high at ~720ms on heavy conc load. We suspect kernel choice and sequence-length spikes cause the p95 tails.
[02:22] Mark: those p95 numbers match what we're seeing in prod spikes, it's the 95th that kills UX.
[02:30] Lina: right, so we ran experiments with three kernel configs: flash-attn tuned, cutlass default, and a quantized-metal path. flash-attn gave best median but had higher variance with long sequences, cutlass was stable but slightly slower, quantized path reduced token compute by ~30% but added decode jitter on TTFT in first token.
[02:58] Priya: wait quantized path affected first token? I thought quantization just impacts throughput.
[03:05] Lina: yeah so in our runtime the quantized kernels currently need an extra dequant step on the first block which adds ~40-60ms to TTFT; after that streaming and batching recover benefits. we're tracking a kernel patch to remove that amortization cost.
[03:25] Mark: can you re-run test with sequence trimming? we found trimming to 512 reduced p95 by 120ms but loses some context.
[03:34] Lina: yes we tested trimming heuristics: left-trim older tokens + prefix caching of conversation state. using a smart trim (keep last 512 + pinned prefix) we hit median 310ms and p95 620ms, so about a 100ms improvement versus baseline.
[03:50] Samir: to clarify for the team — recommended pattern is streaming + flash-attn where sequence lengths are under control, and for long tails use fallback to cutlass or larger dedicated nodes with more stable kernels.
[04:08] Jamal: dedicated nodes mean private deployment or Redwood Dedicated? we need to understand the networking model and KMS integration.
[04:16] Samir: Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud; Redwood Private is VPC/on-prem where you manage KMS and network. For your constraints around HSM/KMS and IP allowlist, Private makes more sense. Dedicated could be used if you can accept our managed KMS with customer-provided keys.
[04:40] Priya: do you have perf diffs between Dedicated and Private? is there an extra latency hit for Private?
[04:47] Lina: not inherently; in Private the latency depends on your infra and network egress. our measurements on equivalent hardware (p4d-ish) show similar kernel perf — the main delta is network hop. we quantify it in the workbook.
[05:05] Anya: back to kernel selection — what's the recommended rollout? do we A/B test kernels?
[05:11] Lina: yes A/B is easiest: canary small percentage on flash-attn, monitor TTFT/p95 and error rates, and auto rollback to cutlass if p95 regresses beyond threshold. Redwood runtime supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
[05:27] Mark: what's the overhead of the automatic fallback — does it interrupt streams?
[05:33] Samir: fallback is per-request routing; ongoing streaming sessions will finish on the node they started, new requests route to fallback. we have graceful degradation heuristics so user-facing sessions maintain consistency.
[05:50] Priya: about batching — you mentioned micro-batches earlier. what's the sweet spot for our workload?
[05:58] Lina: we saw best latency vs throughput trade at micro-batch of 4 requests with continuous batching window of 5-8ms. larger batches improved throughput but added TTFT. we can tune dynamically based on latency SLO.
[06:15] Mark: we typically require 400ms TTFT for interactive flows; background flows can be much higher. can we set per-route SLOs?
[06:22] Samir: yes, per-route SLOs and per-model routing policies are supported — you can route interactive routes to low-latency nodes and background to cost-optimized nodes.
[06:35] Jamal: one more security point — audit logs and token-level traceability. we need full trace of which model/version served which request.
[06:43] Samir: audit logs are supported, including model version, node id, and KMS key id. we'll push the example logs and retention policy to you.
[06:54] Lina: I'll also include the kernel perf artifacts — flame graphs and kernel timing slices. note that the flash-attn build we used had a patch to reduce sync points; without that patch you see worse p95.
[07:09] Priya: how much of this is upstream vs Redwood internal patches — we need to know what we can expect if we go Private and maintain our own runtime.
[07:18] Lina: most of the optimizations are in open-source kernels (flash-attn, cutlass) but we also apply assembly-level tuning and runtime orchestration in Redwood. For Private on-prem we'll provide the tuned runtime and the knobs to adjust kernel selection.
[07:35] Mark: great. can you call out the variance sources so we can instrument them?
[07:40] Lina: sure: 1) sequence length spikes, 2) kernel context-switch syncs, 3) batching window variability, 4) network jitter for Private. instrument model sequence histogram, kernel latency per-block, and batching window histogram.
[07:58] Anya: what's the best way to collect those histograms? do you ship them to your console?
[08:03] Samir: yes console accepts metrics via our agent or agentless ingest; we can set a short retention for the pilot. we'll provide metric names and Grafana dashboard templates.
[08:16] Mark: on p95 reg tests — can we run a synthetic spike run at 3x normal concurrency?
[08:21] Lina: yes we have scripts; we'll run a 3x spike with streaming+trim heuristics and share the logs. expect p95 to rise but we'll quantify.
[08:32] Priya: if p95 still high, is the fallback to a cheaper model variant acceptable? e.g., smaller model for long-tail queries?
[08:38] Samir: absolutely — routing policies can downgrade to a cheaper model variant for non-critical routes. important to validate output quality.
[08:46] Mark: we tried a smaller model earlier and saw hallucination uptick on specific prompts, so need evals tied to prompt sets.
[08:54] Lina: Redwood Optimize can run quality regression checks against your eval set and trigger alerts if rollout causes drop. We'll include that config.
[09:03] Anya: timeline recap?
[09:06] Samir: Samir to share spreadsheet by Friday (2026-10-01). GateBank to provide sample traces and conc profile by 2026-10-03. Lina to run kernel-selection tests on p4d-equivalent env and return perf logs by 2026-10-04. Security docs handoff scheduled by Samir with Jamal.
[09:25] Jamal: one last Q — on KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys or only cloud KMS?
[09:31] Samir: we support customer-managed keys from major cloud KMS and also HSM-backed keys for Private with some integration work; we'll send the integration spec.
[09:44] Mark: ok, thanks everyone. let's reconvene next week same time.
[09:48] Samir: thanks all. end.
